cause: Registering the LMM pack made ordinary shared submission paths executable even though no real C2 OS containment capability had been admitted.
impact: An LMM run could have been evaluated by the host process and misrepresented C1 pinned persistence as C2 execution isolation.
lesson: Shared dispatch and synchronous workflow now reject LMM before any upload, run, or snapshot is materialized; C1 input/result contracts and C2 runtime permission are separate capabilities, so executable model declarations must not imply containment permission.

cause: WO-A tests inserted a manual LMM handler while the production declaration loader owned the same model type, making results depend on suite order.
impact: The full suite failed even though isolated tests passed, obscuring whether Integration had one authoritative model owner.
lesson: Tests exercising a declared pack must use the same declared owner as production; do not shadow a registered model handler in a fixture because loader conflict checks are intentional safety controls.

cause: The release owner has no supported second host now and accepts local development evidence while explicitly deferring real C2 canary validation.
impact: Local development may proceed without an immediate supported containment host; LMM and code execution remain fail-closed and deployment or app packaging still requires C2 host validation.
lesson: A release-owner deferral may change local acceptance status but must not turn unavailable containment into a passing security claim.

lesson: Control operations that update and read the same FMS state must be serialized: append, regenerate retrospective, verify, then promote.

cause: The frontend canonical LMM fixture omitted the execution_binding field that the frozen backend public projection always emits, so the first Table adapter test passed against an impossible packet shape while the browser remained empty.
impact: One full frontend gate and one exact-commit full gate produced false confidence for the visible LMM coefficient surface and had to be repeated after browser discovery.
lesson: Consumer fixtures for versioned packets must be generated from or equality-checked against the backend public projection, including lineage bindings, before they can satisfy an integration gate.

cause: All in-scope local macOS v1.7.3 assembly, automated, known-truth, Agent and browser acceptance gates are complete; hostile-extension containment is explicitly outside this product scope.
impact: The Integration line has one accepted local product baseline and future deployment security work can proceed independently without blocking v1.7.3.
lesson: Close a local release only after a real consumer flow validates cross-lane contracts; keep future trust boundaries in separate work packages rather than shipping unused prototypes.
